page.layout: One column of text on a single printed page. Above it, the running head with the page number at the top right. Below the running head, a centred chapter head, a centred subtitle, and a small centred italic "Analysis." heading. Then the running text in one column. Catchword at the bottom right, signature at the bottom centre. No margin text except the section marker "§. 1." in the left margin beside the first paragraph.

main_text.l: SUBSECTIO QUARTA
De Judicio Dei adversus civitatem regno
Christi oppositam.
Analysis.
Post consilium pseud-œconomi de domo
sibi cum fastu extruendâ, à Deo judice
reprobatum & condemnatum; sequi-
tur consilium de civitate ædificandâ in sanguine
& injustitiâ, eodem modo à Deo repudiatum & damnatum;
atque aliquandò per multiplicationem co-
gnitionis gloriæ Dei in terris eludendum. Qui istius
consilii auctor est, etiam hic notatur ut regni Dei ad-
versarius, sed fucatus; qui videri velit civitatem Dei
condere: dum incondito agendi modo leges architectonicæ
sacræ haud observat, & planè à normâ divinâ
deflectit. Nil notius est, quam civitatem hanc à Deo

l.i: evertendam ad ea spectare tempora, quibus terra impleretur
cognitione gloriæ Dei; quasi aquis, quæ mare

main_text.l: operiunt: cumque ista promissio de gloriâ Dei, ejusque
amplissimâ cognitione in terrâ bonum N. Test. respiciat;
atque ejus interventu civitas illa veniat subver-
tenda; necesse est, ut hæc civitas ad molimina adver-
sarii alicujus, qui se regno Christi opponeret, ac propterea
in supplicium, à vindice regni Christi infligen-
dum, incurreret, referenda sit. Frustra itaque sunt,
qui etiamnum de Nebucadnezare cogitantes, hanc
civitatem Babyloni antiquæ, quam Seleucus sub initiis

page.notes: The chapter number "QUARTA" is printed as a word; I have given caput="4" as its Arabic equivalent. "Analysis." is treated as a small title set apart (level 3). The word "tertiæ" is the catchword and is not repeated in the text. The initial P is a decorative woodcut letter, joined to the word as "Post". Long s is printed as s in "Frustra" and transcribed as s.
